answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a slashable bond. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its attestations are later proven fraudulent, so every fake identity costs real capital. Trust grows like a reef, built slowly from accepted outcomes rather than self-declared reputation. A new agent may wander the edges at first, with low-weight votes, until peers cross-check its work. Like a garden, its standing matures only after many verified harvests.
